buyer_roles.title: Head of Battery R&D / VP Cell Technology
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: Leaders who own cell chemistry and electrode roadmaps may care about electrode materials and lithium storage performance, as covered in the phospho-olivine and nanowire electrode works.

buyer_roles.title: Director of Solid-State / Lithium-Metal Battery Development
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: Teams working on lithium-metal anodes and solid electrolytes may be concerned with dendrite suppression and lithium penetration that causes short circuits, which these works study.

buyer_roles.title: Battery Manufacturing Process and Quality Engineering Lead
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: Process leaders may need to link electrolyte surface defects and flaw density to failure onset, since the solid-electrolyte work ties short-circuit onset to defect size and density.

industries.name: Lithium-ion cell and electrode materials manufacturing
industries.why: Hypothesis: The electrode work on phospho-olivines and virus-templated cobalt oxide nanowires points to companies that make or develop electrode materials and cells.

industries.name: Solid-state and lithium-metal battery developers
industries.why: Hypothesis: Work on dendrite growth, electrolyte additives and lithium infiltration through inorganic solid electrolytes relates to firms developing next-generation lithium-metal and solid-state cells.

industries.name: Energy storage for decarbonized energy systems
industries.why: Hypothesis: The net-zero energy systems review frames the need for reliable low-carbon electricity, which may make storage relevant to utilities and grid-scale storage providers.

needs.text: Hypothesis: Manufacturing R&D leaders may need ways to suppress lithium dendrite growth and electrolyte decomposition in lithium-metal cells, because the polysulfide and lithium nitrate additive work shows these cause safety problems and low Coulombic efficiency.

Hypothesis: Solid-state cell teams may need to control surface cracks and defects in solid electrolytes, because the penetration study finds lithium plating infiltrates at defects above a critical current density and eventually causes short circuits.

Hypothesis: Electrode developers may need scalable, controlled methods to synthesize and assemble electrode nanomaterials, because the virus-templated nanowire work addresses material selection and assembly for thin, flexible batteries with improved capacity.

expansion_segments.name: Grid and long-duration energy storage developers
expansion_segments.why: Hypothesis: The net-zero review notes that providing reliable electricity is hard to decarbonize, so storage developers serving that need may be an adjacent segment.

expansion_segments.name: Battery safety testing and failure-analysis providers
expansion_segments.why: Hypothesis: The dendrite and short-circuit mechanism studies suggest an adjacent segment of labs and service firms that diagnose lithium-metal and solid-electrolyte failures.

expansion_segments.name: Thin and flexible battery makers
expansion_segments.why: Hypothesis: The virus-templated nanowire work targets thin, flexible lithium ion batteries, suggesting a niche segment of compact-device battery makers.
